title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hook and eval metrics export
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We continue to see small but detectible prompt-set regressions slip through PRs that change prompt fixtures or tokenizer preprocessing. This PR adds a CI hook that runs per-prompt evals for the changed prompt sets and wires critical per-prompt metrics into our observability pipeline so regressions become actionable and visible in pull request checks.

What this change does (summary): - Adds a reusable GitHub Actions workflow `prompt-regression.yml` that executes the eval-harness per-prompt CI runner when prompts or eval configs change. The workflow is lightweight by default (sampled runs) and supports an eval matrix for full runs on the release branch. - Implements a new hook module `hooks/prompt_regression_hook.py` which:  * discovers changed prompt ids from the PR diff,  * runs the eval harness for those prompts with deterministic seeds and a small, representative sample,  * computes metrics (accuracy/EM/ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity depending on prompt type),  * compares to baseline thresholds stored in `eval-harness/thresholds/` and fails the job when metrics regress beyond configured deltas, and  * emits metrics to the existing metrics exporter (OTLP/Prometheus) under the `evalh.prompt` namespace. - Metrics and alerting: per-prompt metrics are exported as tags (prompt_id, prompt_set, model_variant) so they surface in the Console dashboards and can be alerted on. Added an example Grafana dashboard JSON and an alert rule (low-sensitivity default) to the docs. - Documentation: updated `docs/ci.md` with setup, thresholds, and how to opt-out for noisy prompts. - Tests: added unit tests for the hook logic and an integration test that runs the hook against a small synthetic prompt set in CI.

Why this approach: Running targeted, per-prompt checks is more cost-effective than running full-suite evals on every PR while still catching regressions that matter. Exporting metrics lets SRE/product own threshold tuning and ties regressions to observable trends.

Checklist: - [x] Add workflow and hook implementation - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Metrics export + example dashboard - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Default thresholds and opt-out mechanisms

Testing and verification: The branch was validated in a feature environment where we introduced a controlled regression in a tokenizer step; the hook correctly flagged the prompt regression and CI failed as expected. All CI checks were rerun after addressing race conditions in the evaluator (see commits).

Rollout plan: Merge to main behind a feature flag (enabled for core-service and eval-harness teams first). Gradually enable organization-wide after one week of monitoring and a couple of post-merge cleanups to thresholds and sampling.

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the threshold config format and the sampling strategy in `prompt_regression_hook.py`. I tried to keep the default conservative to avoid noise; we can relax/improve after empirical runs.

release_notes:
- Add per-prompt regression CI hook to run targeted evals on PRs that change prompts or eval configs.
- Export per-prompt eval metrics to observability (OTLP/Prometheus) so regressions are visible in Console dashboards.
- Default thresholds and opt-out documented in eval-harness/docs/ci.md.
deployment_instructions: Enable feature flag `prompt_regression_ci` in Console for the eval-harness team first. To enable org-wide, update .github/workflows/prompt-regression.yml to remove sampling and add additional matrix entries; tune thresholds in thresholds/<repo>.yaml before enabling.
